result: In 200 young people with acute EBV mononucleosis, 30.1% (55/183) had protracted symptoms and 18.8% (34/181) protracted fatigue at 6 months; prior infection susceptibility (OR 2.98) and severe GI symptoms (OR 3.54) predicted chronic fatigue.
reason: Same post-mono young cohort design, but it measures protracted fatigue rather than paediatric CFS criteria, so it extends (the GI-symptom predictor matches the Jason data in the detail) rather than replicating the CFS rates

result: In 200 young people with acute EBV mononucleosis, severe acute IM symptoms (e.g. severe GI symptoms, OR 3.54) and a history of infection susceptibility (OR 2.98) predicted protracted fatigue at 6 months (18.8%).
reason: EBV only, so it cannot test Dubbo's equal rate across pathogens and does not use CFS criteria; its main result, that acute severity predicts post-infective fatigue, fits immune-sickness-behaviour best

result: In 34.5 million people across 8 databases, the rate of ME/CFS after COVID-19 vs a negative test was higher: IRR 1.22 (1.21-1.23) for ME/CFS symptoms and 1.12 (1.04-1.21) for diagnoses; POTS symptoms IRR 1.24; no rise in autoimmune disease.
reason: Independent, very large cohort with the same measure (ME/CFS incidence after infection vs uninfected) and the same direction, though the effect is far smaller than RECOVER's HR 4.93, in line with the test-negative caveats in the detail

result: In post-COVID cognitive impairment (median 9 months), CSF single-cell RNA showed monocyte recruitment, chemokine signalling and suppressed interferon response in myeloid cells; slow recovery came with higher CSF CXCL8, CCL3L1 and sTREM2 protein; no Alzheimer or neurodegeneration CSF changes.
reason: Long COVID version of CSF immune/chemokine protein differences; it adds a time course, but the subgroup was small and it is not a replication in ME/CFS

result: In post-COVID brain fog, CSF showed myeloid chemokine-signalling and suppressed interferon gene expression, with higher CSF CXCL8, CCL3L1 and sTREM2 protein over follow-up as patients slowly recovered.
reason: Long COVID version of altered CSF chemokines/cytokines; the specific molecules differ from CCL11/IL-1, so it extends rather than replicates

result: In 61 children with long COVID vs 29 healthy controls, 90.2% vs 10.3% had a pathological CPET, with significantly more abnormal peak VO2 (p=0.001), signs of deconditioning and cardiogenic inefficiency.
reason: Same measure and direction, but it adds a paediatric subgroup and uses healthy rather than recovered controls, so extends rather than replicates; 'cardiogenic inefficiency' sits a little uneasily with the finding's non-cardiac interpretation

result: Against a mixed 'aggregate non-healthy' control group (n=17, 14 disorders), only Roseburia and Dialister discriminated ME/CFS without IBS (n=38) by random forest, while many genera discriminated ME/CFS with IBS (n=27).
reason: Adds a specificity test against disease controls that singles out Roseburia, a butyrate producer, but the abstract gives no direction or abundance data and the sample is small

result: Many genera separated ME/CFS with IBS (n=27) from a mixed non-healthy control group, but only Roseburia and Dialister separated ME/CFS without IBS (n=38), suggesting bowel dysfunction drives much of the dysbiosis.
reason: Directly supports IBS status driving the microbiome difference, and adds an illness-in-general control; small samples

result: In 18 people with post-COVID fatigue followed for 12 months, self-rated fatigue impact, peripheral muscle fatigue and autonomic function improved toward control values, and twitch tension rise times became faster than in controls.
reason: Measures peripheral muscle fatigue and twitch properties in post-COVID fatigue, not repeated maximal handgrip in ME/CFS; no other finding fits better than trials-post-covid-course, which the paired link covers

result: Over 12 months, 18 post-COVID fatigue patients improved in fatigue impact, peripheral muscle fatigue and autonomic function, moving toward healthy controls.
reason: Time course in long COVID consistent with improvement in non-ME/CFS post-COVID patients; very small and not stratified by ME/CFS criteria
